title: Painting FAQ: Cost, Timeline, Prep & Warranty
description: Straight answers on house painting cost factors, timelines, prep, products, coats, warranty, and scheduling from a North Central Florida painting contractor.
heroIntro: Homeowners and property managers across North Central Florida ask us the same handful of questions before they hire a painter. Here are our answers.

sections.h2: Why two painting quotes can be so far apart
body: This is the question behind most house painting questions in North Central Florida: why do two bids for the same house differ so much? Usually it's because they cover different work. Bid A pays for a wash, loose paint taken back until the edges hold, a new board where the fascia went soft, fresh sealant in every joint that moves, and a pair of full premium-acrylic coats. Bid B is a single coat rolled over whatever is on the wall today. Both say "paint the exterior," but only one of them will hold up.

Five inputs drive our number: the square footage we measure, how much prep the surfaces need, which product line you pick, how high and reachable the walls are, and how many colors are involved. Color itself hardly changes the price. Condition changes it a lot. Chalky siding, mildew on a shaded wall, or rot at a window sill all add labor, and a quote that leaves them out is cheaper because it does less.

sections.h2: How long painting takes, and when to book it
body: Count on roughly one working day per interior room. Repainting every room in a house can take as little as three days or as long as two weeks. A whole exterior is a three-to-seven-working-day paint job once washing is finished and the walls have dried out. After you approve an estimate, the start date is usually one to three weeks away.

Season matters more outside than inside. The calmest months for exterior house painting here run from October to May. Summer exterior crews begin soon after dawn, and their lead rechecks dew point readings and the weather radar as the heat climbs. For the long version, read how Florida weather affects painting. Interiors can be painted any month.

sections.h2: Questions about products, coats, and prep
body: Our floor is two full coats. A third gets added if you are going from navy to cream, say, or if the surface is so porous it soaks up the first coat. Products follow the substrate: 100% acrylic for siding and outside trim, elastomeric for stucco with movement, waterborne urethane enamel where cabinets, doors, and railings take daily handling, and a penetrating stain for raw wood. Torn between eggshell and satin? Our room-by-room guide to choosing a paint finish for each room compares them.

Repairs are part of prep, not an extra. That includes nail pops, drywall patches, rotted trim, and failed caulk. Every one of those repairs shows up as its own line on the estimate, so none of it gets buried under fresh paint.

sections.h2: Questions about living with the project
body: Most homeowners stay home during an interior repaint. Our painters shift and drape the furniture, cover the floors, and stick to one room at a time, which keeps the rest of the house livable. If odor is a concern, for example with a nursery, a home office, or someone sensitive to smells, we can use low-VOC options. Commercial projects can run on nights and weekends so staff and customers aren't affected.

For exterior work, we'll ask you to move cars away from the walls and keep pets inside on spray days. Expect a wash day before painting starts, then a pause while everything dries. That gap is part of the plan. Painting damp siding in humid weather leads to early peeling.

sections.h2: Get everything in writing, whoever you hire
body: Our advice applies to any painter you're considering, us included. Ask for surfaces included and excluded, prep steps, product line, number of coats, and warranty terms in writing. A one-page scope like that prevents most disputes before they happen. Our free written estimates include all of it. Still have a question this page did not cover? Get in touch and a crew lead will answer it.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to paint a house in North Central Florida?
faqs.a: There is no published price list, because surface condition swings the number more than anything else. Your price comes from the measured area, the prep and repairs needed, the product line, how high and accessible the work is, and how many colors you choose. A free walkthrough produces an itemized, written figure.

faqs.q: Do I need to move furniture or leave the house?
faqs.a: No. Leave the heavy lifting to the crew: they carry and cover the furniture and paint one room at a time, so you can keep living at home while the inside is repainted.

faqs.q: Can you match an existing color?
faqs.a: Yes. A chip from the hardware store, a cabinet door off its hinges, or the half-empty can from when the house was last painted all work as a source. We tint to it, brush a full-size drawdown, and paint nothing until you have approved that sample.

Yes. Exterior workmanship is backed by a written warranty lasting as long as 10 years; the manufacturer separately warrants its paint. Problems spotted on the final walkthrough are corrected before we close the job, and you keep labelled cans of each color for future touch-ups.
